answer: Sequential Work Witness: each identity must publish a hash chain of completed microtasks whose timing matches a measured compute-latency ridge for the claimed hardware. Chains are cross-checked against random peers, and only chains older than a fixed age can transact. An attacker must actually run every task on real hardware, paying wall-clock time and electricity per identity, and cannot fork a vine of fake histories without diverging from observable latency. Cost scales with elapsed time, not money, so mass registration stalls on the tundra of idle capacity.
